skill_friction: Tier thresholds are undefined anywhere in the org. They are values, not components, so under Step 5 they do not change the inventory and cannot justify a question. But without them the main responsibility cannot be delivered. The skill has no guidance on whether a missing business parameter like this should trigger a question or become a Conditional row with placeholders. I chose Conditional with placeholders and marked it blocking for delivery.

Keeping thresholds in the flow versus a custom metadata type does change the inventory. Neither the requirement nor the org evidence settles it, but Rule 4 (minimal design) points to the flow. It is unclear whether Rule 4 counts as 'evidence' that lets the agent skip the question.

The Redeem sign convention for Points__c cannot be observed because the org has 0 transaction rows. The skill's data-shape check gives no fallback when there is no data. I used ABS() to handle both conventions and recorded it as an assumption.

AskCoworker labelled facts that came from my own 'Established so far' bullets as '[Verified: prior session]'. The skill's rule on echoed facts covers this, but the label makes it hard to tell echoed facts from real prior-session memory.

R proposed granting FLS on the new fields to five existing permission sets, three of them non-editable sfdcInternalInt sets. The spec-format rule against widening broad permission sets resolved this, but the skill does not say whether a derived, system-maintained field that nobody is required to see needs any access row at all.
Before-save flows reading formula and roll-up values during a roll-up-driven parent save is platform behavior that no allowed query can test. It stays an assumption, with a test and a fallback.
